data.title: Acarbose, 17-alpha-estradiol, and nordihydroguaiaretic acid extend mouse lifespan preferentially in males
data.authors: Harrison DE; Miller RA et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Beyond rapamycin, the same ITP program found acarbose extended male median lifespan by 22% - evidence that the registry surfaces real positive hits too, not only negative results.
data.abstract_excerpt: Four agents--acarbose (ACA), 17-α-estradiol (EST), nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA), and methylene blue (MB)--were evaluated for lifespan effects in genetically heterogeneous mice tested at three sites. Acarbose increased male median lifespan by 22% (P < 0.0001), but increased female median lifespan by only 5% (P = 0.01). This sexual dimorphism in ACA lifespan effect could not be explained by differences in effects on weight. Maximum lifespan (90th percentile) increased 11% (P < 0.001) in males and 9% (P = 0.001) in females.

extracted_findings.effect: Acarbose extended male median lifespan by 22% (female 5%); EST and NDGA extended lifespan preferentially in males
extracted_findings.dose: Acarbose at 1000 mg kg −1 diet (1000 ppm) from 4 months of age
extracted_findings.effect_size: Male median lifespan increased by 22% (P < 0.0001); female median lifespan increased by 5% (P = 0.01) (pooled data).
